status_observed: 500 {"detail": "Internal server error"} â€” for a duplicate email AND for every invalid foreign key (department_id, designation_id, employment_type_id, reporting_manager_id, work_location_address_id) and for a non-UUID id string
what_is_wrong: Every database integrity failure on employee creation escapes as an unhandled 500 instead of the 409 the code intends. The INSERT is executed by `await db.flush()` at app/api/v1/employees.py:245, which sits OUTSIDE the `try: await db.commit() except DBAPIError: ... _as_client_error(...)` block at lines 267-271, so the IntegrityError is raised before the handler can ever see it. Proof it is the flush and not a missing handler: PUT /api/v1/employees/{id} has the identical handler but no flush, and returns a clean 409 for the exact same violations. Real-world impact: HR re-entering an employee whose email already exists, or a stale department id in a form, gets a bare 500 with no indication of what was wrong.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/employees.py:245 (`await db.flush()` outside the try/except DBAPIError at lines 267-271)

status_observed: 500 {"detail": "Internal server error"} â€” but the state change was already committed; the immediate retry returns 409 {"detail": "Welcome email already sent"}
what_is_wrong: The endpoint half-completes and then throws. It commits employees.welcome_email_sent_at and sets the SEND_WELCOME_EMAIL onboarding item to COMPLETE, sends the email, then calls notify(..., notification_type="EMPLOYEE") and does a second `await db.commit()` with no exception handler. The notifications table's ck_notif_type CHECK constraint does not allow the value 'EMPLOYEE' (allowed: LEAVE, DOCUMENT, PAYSLIP, TICKET, TASK, ASSET, PROFILE_CHANGE, ANNOUNCEMENT, COMPENSATORY_HOURS, ONBOARDING, EXIT, TAX_DECLARATION, CREDIT_NOTE, EXPENSE), so the commit raises and becomes a 500. Consequences: (a) HR sees a hard server error on an action that actually ran, (b) the onboarding step is permanently stuck as COMPLETE and cannot be re-run (409 forever), (c) the employee never receives the in-app welcome notification the code intends to create. Verified in the DB after the 500: onboarding_checklist_items row SEND_WELCOME_EMAIL = COMPLETE and employees.welcome_email_sent_at = 2026-08-26 06:56:05. The email itself did dispatch (email_send_log row 36b3379e-9aa7-47cd-994f-d496aaf80be1, 'Welcome to Meshrd, Zedd'), so this is not an SMTP problem. NOTE: this path is onboarding-lifecycle and may belong to the other employee agent; reporting it because it is a live 500 on an endpoint tagged 'employee'.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/employee_lifecycle.py:315 â€” `notification_type="EMPLOYEE"` violates the notifications.ck_notif_type CHECK; the following `await db.commit()` (line ~318) is unguarded

what_is_wrong: The employee email field has no format validation at all â€” the schema declares `email: str` rather than pydantic's EmailStr, and there is no DB CHECK on it either. A record was created and persisted with the literal value 'not-an-email' and it read back identically through GET /api/v1/employees/{id}. This is the login identity for the employee: POST /{id}/create-login copies employee.email verbatim into users.email, and create-login / reset-password / send-welcome-email all dispatch the temporary password to that address. An HR typo therefore produces a permanently unreachable login whose password can never be delivered. Contrast with the same module's other fields, which ARE constrained at the DB level (emergency contact phone regex ^[6-9][0-9]{9}$, relationship enum, document_type enum) â€” email is the outlier.
suspected_cause: app/schemas/employee.py:18 â€” `email: str` in EmployeeWrite (should be EmailStr); no CHECK constraint on employees.email either

status_observed: 409 {"detail": "Only one contact may be marked Primary"} returned for a body where is_primary is false â€” the actual violation was the `relationship` value or the `contact_phone` format
what_is_wrong: The 409 detail message is hardcoded to one specific constraint but is used as the catch-all for every DBAPIError on this table. employee_emergency_contacts carries three CHECK constraints (ck_eec_relationship: SPOUSE|PARENT|SIBLING|FRIEND|OTHER; ck_eec_phone: ^[6-9][0-9]{9}$; ck_eec_name: non-blank) plus the one-primary unique index, and all four collapse into the same misleading sentence. Sending relationship="Brother" with is_primary=false tells the operator they may only have one primary contact, which is both false and unactionable. Compounding it, neither the relationship enum nor the phone pattern appears in the OpenAPI contract (`relationship` and `contact_phone` are declared as plain nullable strings), so a client has no way to know the accepted values. The same shape applies to POST .../documents, where document_type is a plain string in the spec but is constrained by ck_ed_type to ID_PROOF|EDUCATIONAL_CERTIFICATE|RESUME|OFFER_LETTER_COPY|OTHER.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/employees.py:727 and :752 â€” `_as_client_error(exc, "Only one contact may be marked Primary")` used as the generic fallback for all DBAPIErrors on this table

what_is_wrong: Any second tax-scheme election for an employee in the same Financial Year returns 500, so an employee's tax scheme can never be changed once one is on record. The endpoint inserts the new election row and only afterwards stamps superseded_at on the old one; between those two statements both rows carry the same generated current_guard value, violating UNIQUE KEY ux_etse_current. That INSERT happens at an unguarded db.flush(), so the IntegrityError escapes the try/except that wraps only the commit.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/tax_declarations.py:131 â€” db.add(row) then `await db.flush()` runs before `previous.superseded_at` is set (lines 132-135), and the flush sits outside the try/except DBAPIError that starts at line 136. Unique key: alembic/versions/0003_employee_leave.py:1619 `UNIQUE KEY ux_etse_current (current_guard)` over the generated column at line 1614.

The duplicate is caught by a unique constraint during db.flush(), which is outside the try/except that wraps commit â€” so the handler's own message "A Tax Declaration for this Financial Year already exists" is unreachable dead code.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/tax_declarations.py:186 â€” `await db.flush()` after db.add(declaration) is outside the try/except DBAPIError at lines 218-222 whose fallback message is "A Tax Declaration for this Financial Year already exists".

status_observed: 200, but the exit checklist and settlement workflow stay fully live afterwards
what_is_wrong: Withdrawing a resignation only flips resignations.status to WITHDRAWN (and un-does ON_NOTICE). It does not cancel or lock the exit checklist rows. After withdrawal HR can still generate and send a Resignation Acceptance Letter for that resignation, complete exit checklist steps, and drive the final settlement from NOT_DUE to DUE to PAID on a resignation the employee retracted. (The final EXITED transition is separately blocked by a DB trigger that excludes WITHDRAWN resignations, so the employee is not terminated â€” but everything up to that point proceeds.)

status_observed: 201, but lta_amount is silently dropped whenever lta_payout_basis is ANNUAL
what_is_wrong: lta_payout_basis accepts 'ANNUAL' (it is one of the two values allowed by CHECK ck_ss_lta_basis) and lta_amount is persisted and echoed back, but the value then affects nothing: it is excluded from gross_monthly, and since annual_ctc is derived from gross_monthly it is excluded from annual_ctc too, and payroll only emits an LTA earning line when the basis is MONTHLY. An annual LTA entered by HR is therefore stored, displayed, and never paid or costed.
suspected_cause: app/services/salary_engine.py:77 `lta_component = lta_amount if lta_payout_basis == "MONTHLY" else Decimal("0")`; annual_ctc at app/services/salary_engine.py:104-109 is built from gross_monthly and never re-adds an annual LTA; app/api/v1/payroll_runs.py:298 only emits the LTA line `if structure.lta_payout_basis == "MONTHLY"`. A repo-wide grep for lta_amount finds no other consumer.

status_observed: 200 [] for a date range that contains two matching rows
what_is_wrong: The posted_on_to filter compares a DATETIME column against a date, which MySQL coerces to midnight, so the end of the range is exclusive of the day the user named. Filtering "posted on 26 Aug" for announcements published at 06:50 on 26 Aug returns nothing; only posted_on_to=2026-08-27 finds them. Any HR user filtering an announcement feed up to today gets an empty or short list.
